scenes.tts: Four men had sperm that could not swim. Three of them also could not clear mucus from their airways. Under the electron microscope, their cilia lacked small projections called dynein arms. One missing part caused two failures in two organs. A sperm tail and an airway cilium must share a machine.
scenes.visual: Sperm tail and airway cilium each crossed out, both pointing to a question-mark box; the box opens to the cilium cross-section with the arms missing.
scenes.narration: Four men had sperm that could not swim. Three of them also could not clear mucus from their airways. Under the electron microscope, their cilia lacked small projections called dynein arms. One missing part caused two failures in two organs. A sperm tail and an airway cilium must share a machine.

scenes.tts: Sperm tails and airway cilia are built on the same axoneme. It is a cylinder of microtubules. In the classic pattern, nine outer doublets surround a central pair. Each doublet is a complete A-tubule with an incomplete B-tubule fused to it. The whole cylinder grows from a basal body, which anchors it in the cell.
scenes.visual: Cross-section builds: nine doublets, then the central pair, then one doublet zoomed to show A and B tubules; side view with basal body.
scenes.caption: Sperm tails and airway cilia are built on the same axoneme. It is a cylinder of microtubules. In the classic pattern, nine outer doublets surround a central pair. Each doublet is a complete A-tubule with an incomplete B-tubule fused to it. The whole cylinder grows from a basal body, which anchors it in the cell.
scenes.narration: Sperm tails and airway cilia are built on the same axoneme. It is a cylinder of microtubules. In the classic pattern, nine outer doublets surround a central pair. scenes.tts: Along each A-tubule sit two rows of dynein arms, the outer and inner arms. These are the arms that the four men lacked. Each motor head acts on the B-tubule of the next doublet. It walks toward that tubule's minus end, at the base. So each doublet pushes its neighbour toward the tip.
scenes.visual: Two doublets drawn as long bars; arms on the lower bar grip the upper bar and push it toward the tip.
scenes.narration: Along each A-tubule sit two rows of dynein arms, the outer and inner arms. These are the arms that the four men lacked. Each motor head acts on the B-tubule of the next doublet. It walks toward that tubule's minus end, at the base. So each doublet pushes its neighbour toward the tip.

scenes.tts: Why does pushing make a bend? Think of two neighbouring doublets as two strips of card, side by side. They are glued together at one end and tied loosely along their length. Push one strip toward the far end. The pair cannot slide apart, so it curves.
scenes.visual: Two card strips glued at the left and tied along their length; the top strip is pushed and the pair curves.
scenes.narration: Why does pushing make a bend? Think of two neighbouring doublets as two strips of card, side by side. They are glued together at one end and tied loosely along their length. Push one strip toward the far end. The pair cannot slide apart, so it curves.

scenes.tts: In the axoneme, the base is anchored and the links resist. So shear between doublets becomes a bend. Summers and Gibbons took the resistance away. They digested sea urchin sperm axonemes briefly with trypsin, and added A T P. Seen by dark-field microscopy, the doublets slid apart. Dynein does not shorten microtubules. It slides them.
scenes.visual: The two doublets bend as the arms push; then trypsin cuts the links and the pushed doublet slides straight out.
scenes.caption: In the axoneme, the base is anchored and the links resist. So shear between doublets becomes a bend. Summers and Gibbons took the resistance away. They digested sea-urchin sperm axonemes briefly with trypsin, and added ATP. Seen by dark-field microscopy, the doublets slid apart. Dynein does not shorten microtubules. It slides them.

scenes.tts: This gives a test for a paralysed flagellum. Isolate the axonemes, cut the links, and add A T P. If the doublets slide apart, the motors work. Then the fault lies in regulating them, or in turning sliding into bending. The radial spokes, the central pair, and the nexin dynein regulatory complex are the places to look. If they do not slide, suspect missing or inactive dynein arms. A bend is sliding that the links resist.
scenes.visual: Test with two outcomes: slides apart means motors work, look at spokes, central pair and links; no sliding means arms missing or inactive.
